name: Berry Red
lede: Berry Red is a deep purplish red; as a screen value it is identical to X11's maroon.

sections.title: A berry word
sections.body: The library finds the color in Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary and in lists drawn from Wikipedia and a Japanese-name source [1]. The nearest ISCC-NBS category is strong purplish red, about 4 units away [1]. The same hex is listed as [[maroon-x11]], at zero distance [2]. Close neighbors are [[rubellite]], [[amaranth-purple]] and [[raspberry]] [2]. The swatch has a lightness of 41.5 on a 100 scale, so it is a mid-dark red with a purple lean [1]. Raspberry sits 5.8 units off [2]. The books we hold do not discuss the name itself, so its origin is generic: the red of berries [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Only 6 paintings in our archive of 23,781 hold this color, as photographed, which makes it rarer than 77% of named colors [3]. The earliest is dated to about 1900 [3]. The phrase peaks in printed English in the 1820s, and rose fastest in the 1920s, though it covers any berry-red thing [4]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, not pigment tests.
